tldr: SELF-REFINE is an iterative self-refinement algorithm where a single LLM generates an initial output, provides feedback on it, and refines itself using that feedback, improving outputs across diverse tasks without additional training.
contributions: Introducing SELF-REFINE, an iterative refinement approach that uses a single LLM as generator, refiner, and feedback provider without requiring supervised training data or reinforcement learning
Demonstrating consistent improvements across 7 diverse tasks including dialogue generation, code optimization, math reasoning, and constrained generation
Showing that even state-of-the-art LLMs like GPT-4 can be further improved at test-time using this simple standalone approach
methods: SELF-REFINE starts by generating an initial output using an LLM M given input x and a few-shot prompt p_gen. The same model M then provides feedback f_b on its own output using a feedback prompt p_fb, generating specific and actionable feedback. The model then refines the output using the feedback with a refinement prompt p_refine. This feedback-REFINE cycle iterates up to 4 times until a stopping condition is met, with previous outputs and feedback appended to maintain history.
results: SELF-REFINE consistently improves over base models across all tasks. GPT-4+SELF-REFINE achieved absolute improvements of 21.6-49.2% in preference-based tasks: Sentiment Reversal (30.4 to 36.2), Dialogue Response Generation (25.4 to 74.6, +49.2), Code Optimization (27.3 to 36.0, +8.7), Acronym Generation (30.4 to 56.0, +25.6), and Constrained Generation (15.0 to 45.0, +30.0). Average improvement across all tasks was ~20% absolute. Improvement was consistent across GPT-3.5, ChatGPT, and GPT-4. Specific actionable feedback was crucial: removing it caused significant performance drops, and generic feedback performed worse than specific feedback.
limitations: Math Reasoning showed only modest gains because LLMs struggle to accurately identify nuanced errors in their own reasoning chains; 94% of ChatGPT feedback was 'everything looks good'
Weaker models like Vicuna-13B struggled significantly with the refinement process, failing to generate feedback in the required format and often repeating outputs or hallucinating instead of refining
Diminishing returns occur with more iterations, and in multi-aspect tasks, quality can vary during iteration with improvement in one aspect but decline in another
